idiom_name: Array.prototype.filter (copy-out) or write-index compaction + arr.length = n
implementation_notes: JavaScript arrays expose no in-place bulk removal: the idiomatic answer is Array.prototype.filter(pred), which 'creates a shallow copy of a portion of a given array, filtered down to just the elements from the given array that pass the test implemented by the provided function' in one pass, and the caller rebinds the reference to that new array. That is copy-out: aliases keep the old contents and peak memory doubles, so when the array must keep its identity (it is referenced elsewhere or is a hot buffer) the idiom is written out - a write index copies survivors down, then arr.length = n truncates, which is one pass plus one length update with no allocation. splice is the per-range tool and shifts the tail on every call, so calling it per element is the O(n^2) anti-pattern this pattern replaces, and delete arr[i] leaves a hole rather than shortening the array.
pitfalls: filter returns a new array: rebinding (rows = rows.filter(...)) leaves every other reference to the old array untouched, and that old array keeps the removed elements alive.

filter skips holes in sparse arrays (its callback 'is invoked only for array indexes which have assigned values'), so a sparse array comes back dense and its length can shrink in ways delete-based code did not expect.

splice inside a forward loop shifts the tail and renumbers the remaining elements (the next index is skipped), while delete arr[i] leaves undefined holes instead of shortening the array - both look like removal but are not the compaction.
TypedArray.prototype.filter also copies (and returns the same typed-array kind), so binary buffers need the same manual compaction; there is no in-place filter anywhere in the language.
sources: MDN, Array.prototype.filter() - 'creates a shallow copy of a portion of a given array, filtered down to just the elements from the given array that pass the test implemented by the provided function'; the callback is invoked only for indexes with assigned values: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/filter
